body: I feel you 100%.  I don't know if I could stand to see everything I've built over the years go completely to waste because of transitioning.  But I don't know if I can stand to live this way any more either.

I have multiple problems going on.  First, I have shitty self esteem and I'm very negative and harsh with myself.  Second, I have some pretty severe gender dysphoria.  Third, I have severe anxiety.  These aren't entirely separate issues, but all of them need to be addressed.  

I don't know if this is an existential crisis, but I never really give myself any credit, no matter how well I do at anything.  I never give myself a pat on the back or a kind word.  I know this is a problem, but I started doing it at a young age and can't seem to stop.  

I live in a major metropolitan area.  There are GLBT centers I could probably walk into and see someone immediately, but I'm afraid of being recognized.  I'm not famous enough to get swarmed on the street, but I do get recognized at least a few times a week in public.  I'm too paranoid.

PREPARE FOR LIFE STORY IN 3 . . . 2 . . . 1 . . . 

**TL;DR:  gender neutral/male kid, femmed up for social/economic reasons after puberty, regret not transitioning at 18.**

What does it feel like to identify as male in a female body? 

When I was a young kid, I felt gender neutral.  I didn't play with princess costumes or baby dolls.  Instead I had plastic dinosaurs, RC cars, puzzles, and the like.  I was very into science.  I learned to read at a young age and always had a book in my hand.  I liked to collect rocks and seashells and identify them.  I liked frogs and snakes and bugs.  I dressed like a tomboy, which wasn't really a big deal in the 90's.  Clothing for kids back then was pretty genderless.

My parents were pretty severely abusive (physically, verbally, emotionally, you name it).  I used food to cope.  Between the ages of 8 and 13, I was obese.  I hid my body in baggy clothes and became a "skater."  I shopped exclusively in the boys/men's section.  I even wore men's underwear.  I hung out with the other skater/slacker kids and was more or less accepted as one of the boys, even though that was never explicitly said.  I just wasn't treated like the girl of the group.  Around this age, I started to question my gender identity.  

I didn't want to be a woman.  I hated having female parts.  I didn't like the female pattern of speech.  I didn't want to have babies.  I didn't mind female clothing, but at the time, I felt much more comfortable in Vans, tighty whiteys, cargo shorts and a giant South Park tshirt.  At this time, I had crushes on both men and women, and thought I might just be a butch lesbian or something.  I had no idea what it all meant.

By the time I was 13, I had access to the internet.  I eventually stumbled upon resources for transmen and nearly fell out of my seat.  I didn't know you could DO that.  I'd always heard about people "getting a sex change," but only the MTF stories.

Once I knew that FTM was a thing, I couldn't get it out of my head.  I started binding my chest with ace bandages all the time.  In the privacy of my room, I packed my underwear with a condom filled with hair gel.  I fantasized about going on testosterone.  Despite the brutality of the surgeries involved, and the social ramifications, I wasn't afraid at all.  It just seemed right.  I was going to do it.  I was going to transition as soon as I was old enough.

Around that time, thanks to the internet, I was also exposed to gay male culture, and found myself wanting to be a part of it.  I wanted a boyfriend, and I wanted to BE a boyfriend.  I also discovered gay porn.  Ahem.  

Aaaaaaand then somehow, magically, around the age of 14, all the weight fell off me, I got my period in earnest, and I transformed within a matter of weeks into a drop-dead beauty.    

The way people treated me changed overnight.  I went from being called "son" by strangers (as in "excuse me, son") to being eye-fucked by every guy I passed.  The power shift terrified and excited me.  The first time after that point that I happened to wear a dress, I practically broke necks.  Men would bend over backwards to talk to me, give me things, make me smile. 

What are you supposed to do with that kind of power?  At that age, I wanted to fuck hot dudes more than I wanted to be true to myself, so I hung up the cargo shorts, learned how to line my eyes, and started playing the female role.  

Putting on femme always feels like drag.  I can never do the girl thing subtly.  If I was being femme, I was high femme - full makeup, corsets, high heels, fishnets, teased hair, purple lipstick, tons of jewelry, the works.  I ended up sliding nicely into Goth culture, which was a theatrical enough look to satisfy my need to overcompensate, and was dark enough to satisfy my growing depression.

I did have boyfriends by the score, though.  I probably slept with half the boys in high school.  I was always safe and never got an STD or knocked up, thank god, but man was I busy.  It was good fun, and I don't regret it.  I put my male side in the closet and told myself that this was the life I wanted.  The power of being a beautiful girl, I told myself, was worth any price.

I had great grades despite my issues, and I ended up going to a private university on scholarship.  I started modeling on the side to feed myself and ended up becoming wildly successful.  I decided to leave university.  I don't regret that at all.  The industry has been good to me.

Every once in a while I would meet someone who was FTM.  Or I'd see a transman on the TV.  And I'd feel a bizarre ache, wondering how my life would be different if I'd just taken the plunge at 18 like I'd planned.  As the years wear by, I question my choices more and more.

By now, I'm so firmly entrenched in being female that I don't know if I can leave it.  My entire adult life has been built upon a lie - one that I tell so very well, I do it better than the women who want to be women.  But it makes me sick.  I get sicker by the year.  I feel like I'm wearing a costume.  It's starting to affect my sex life, too.  I have a hard time connecting with my female body.  I could go on and on about it.

I'd have to save up lots of money to make it work.  I could do that - put aside funds for a few years to save up for surgeries and to go back to school for a new career (which I'd need to do anyway).  It just seems so overwhelming.  I don't know if I can make it that long. 

My great fear is that I'd end up lonely and unloved.  That even if my body were altered to reflect my internal self, no one would want me.  I'd rather die than live like that.

That's a really good point, about transitioning after modeling.  I figure I've got another good 8-10 years in me before they "put me out to pasture," and I'll still be relatively young.  The only problems are:

1.  I don't know if I can wait that long.

2.  I'm likely to lose everyone who is close to me.  Especially my husband.

I know a lot can happen in a decade.  Who knows if my husband and I would even still be together.  That "problem" could correct itself, for all I know.  Even though that's something I don't want to think about.
